author: kevaundray

- 8 threads reserved

- AVX2 needed, AVX512 preferred

author: arnetheduck
content: now, eip 7870 says "8c / 16t" for builder - that's a 5 -year old cpu _more or less_ in my book .. if you take 8 threads from that, it leaves 8 "fake" threads for running other things .. so in that equation, you're actually getting 8 half-threads

author: arnetheduck
content: hyperthreading works with scheduling tricks - depending on what else is going on, ie which parts of the cpu "the other" things needs, you're actually taking up "the whole" cpu with your "8 threads reserved", if the other things involve the same logic units.

author: kevaundray

author: arnetheduck
content: well, hyperthreading is tricky - the whole point of it is that adding load lets the cpu do better scheduling and pipelining, but if you stuff the pipeline you don't actually get anything from it .. in some workloads, it's actually _better_ to disable HT and have fewer "fake" cores

author: arnetheduck
content:
an option I _tend to_ like is a system that has built-in elasticity to degrade gracefully .. it's easy to build a system that works well under optimal conditions but then goes into a death spiral under stress - this is something we often see in testnets for example, due to various reasons (mostly because we rarely test the "stressed" case and therefore don't spend as much time on ironing out bugs) ..

so for crypto, I would consider it a key feature that work is done incrementally and that "partial progress" still can be used, albeit with degraded rewards for example - degraded is better than nothing in stress scenarios because it can better get the system as a whole out of it .. 

in bls for example, we can play with latency vs cpu by batch-validating more signatures - on a weak cpu, we can do larger batches and still participate meaningfully

author: arnetheduck
